text:
deploy-bot: Pager: Canary pool 'staged-v2' reporting 7xx rate 42% above threshold for the last 3m. Affected region: us-west-2. Triggered by rollout 2026-03-15T02:45Z. @alex (oncall) paging now.

alex (oncall): seeing increased 502/504s and timeouts on the canary. latency up too. I'm on it.

maya (runtime): confirmed - the kernel worker logs show scheduler queue spikes and OOM-shim restarts on 3 hosts. `kube-node-rt-{12,14,19}`.

sam (release): rolling traffic was at 10% canary -> 25% 10m ago due to staged policy. We didn't change model variant. Only infra-level flag: `enable_scheduler_v2=true` in the rollout config.

jess (infra): pulling node metrics now. Node-level CPU+io wait correlated with scheduling spikes. suspect the new scheduler path is pinning threads.

alex (oncall): customer impact? any external errors surfaced? lia (support) - can you surface top customer errors?

lia (support): seeing elevated error rates in our SRE dashboard and multiple support tickets for timeouts on generate endpoints. 4 customers with high volume impacted (two enterprise). Sending a short PSAT.

ops-bot: auto-annotate: incident-severity=high, mitigation-status=investigating, escalation=oncall.

maya (runtime): quick sanity check: `kubectl logs` shows repeated "kv cache miss loop" and scheduler backoff message. Not pure OOM, looks like lock contention in scheduler v2 path.

sam (release): we have a fast rollback option: flip rollout traffic back to v1 via rollout-service or flip feature flag `enable_scheduler_v2=false`. Which is faster?

jess (infra): flipping fflag is fast (propagates in <30s to control-plane), but some steady-state nodes still running v2 until drain. Rolling back the canary traffic to 0% will remove impact immediately.

alex (oncall): prioritize traffic kill-switch. sam - can you flip the traffic stage? I'll prepare the flag flip as fallback.

sam (release): doing staged rollback now: `rolloutctl set-traffic staged-v2 0% --reason "scheduler contention"`

deploy-bot: Executing rolloutctl request. Step 1/3: update control-plane routes.

maya (runtime): heads up - if we drop traffic, some in-flight sessions might see 502s for a short window. prepare customer comms.

deploy-bot: Step 2/3: routes updated. Traffic to staged-v2 is now 0%. Observability note added.

alex (oncall): monitoring metrics... host queue depth dropping, request error rate falling.

jess (infra): Node CPU and io-wait normalizing across the cluster. No new OOM-shim restarts.

lia (support): error rates for affected customers dropping. Support will escalate ticket priority and send an interim update: "We detected a regression in a staged rollout and have routed traffic away while we investigate."

maya (runtime): collecting kernel logs and stack traces from the offending nodes. saving core dumps to /artifacts/canary-scheduler-1747604321.tar.gz.

sam (release): flipping feature flag as safe fallback: `ffctl set enable_scheduler_v2 false --env staged --note "emergency rollback"`

deploy-bot: FF update accepted, propagation to control-plane nodes in progress.

alex (oncall): handoff plan: I'm going to do a 30m post-mortem with runtime+infra. @sam please coordinate a rollback PR to revert scheduler_v2 commit if we confirm root cause. @maya collect repro steps. @lia prepare customer follow-up for the enterprise accounts.

ops-bot: incident-update: mitigation=traffic-routed-away, next-step=postmortem, severity-assessment=customer-impact-medium-high.

maya (runtime): initial triage: regression introduced a new lock on the scheduling loop that scales poorly under high fanout. reproducing with a load test that mimics canary traffic now.

jess (infra): long-term: we'll add a canary health probe for scheduler queue depth and an autoscaling tweak to limit node-level fanout. Filing infra ticket INFRA-2026-83.

sam (release): rolling rollback PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pull/487 - includes revert and extra telemetry for scheduler path.

lia (support): interim customer message drafted and shared in #customer-comm for approval.

alex (oncall): last check: error rate back to baseline for 5m. I'm demoting pager to passive watch. If we see re-escalation, page me immediately.

deploy-bot: Pager resolved by user action at 1747604830.

alex (oncall): thanks all. We'll meet in 30m for a quick blameless follow-up. I'll update the incident tracker with timeline and impacted customers.

maya (runtime): saving traces and linking to the postmortem doc. will upload artifacts and repro steps.

sam (release): note for postmortem: improve pre-rollout load test to include scheduler edge-case scenario.

lia (support): will send targeted customer follow-ups in ~45m after postmortem summary.

jess (infra): moving INFRA-2026-83 to priority-high.

ops-bot: incident-closed-note queued for the incident tracker.

alex (oncall): closing thread here. If anyone has additions, append to the incident tracker. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
